title_ar: قانون رقم (13) لسنة 2016 بشأن حماية خصوصية البيانات الشخصية
edition_version: Promulgated 3 Nov 2016 (3/2/1438H); 32 articles; newspaper reproduction dated 3 Nov 2016
title: Law No. (13) of 2016 on the Protection of Personal Data Privacy (Qatar) - full Arabic text as published by Al-Sharq
authors: State of Qatar (Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani)
publisher: Al-Sharq (Doha) - reproduction of the promulgated text
key_findings: Art. 4: processing only with the individual's consent unless necessary for a legitimate purpose of the controller or recipient; Art. 5: withdrawal of consent, objection, erasure and correction rights.

Art. 16: 'personal data of a special nature' expressly includes data relating to CHILDREN (with ethnic origin, health, religion, marital relationship, criminal offences); processing requires a permit from the competent department under ministerial rules.

Art. 17: operators of websites directed at children must post a notice, obtain the express consent of the child's guardian (electronically or by other suitable means), give the guardian on request a description and copy of the child's data, delete or stop processing on the guardian's request, and not condition a child's participation in a game, prize or activity on more data than necessary.

Art. 14: controller must notify the individual and the competent department of any breach of safeguards likely to cause serious damage (no hour limit in the Law itself); Art. 13: processor must notify the controller immediately.
Art. 15: the controller may not take measures that restrict cross-border data flows unless the processing breaches the Law or would cause serious damage - i.e. the Law itself is transfer-permissive.
Arts. 23-25: fines up to QAR 1 million (Arts. 4, 8-12, 14, 15, 22) and up to QAR 5 million for breaches of Art. 13, Art. 16(3) and Art. 17; Art. 30: six months to regularise, extendable.
athar_applications: Qatar: treat all child users' data as special-nature data needing a permit from the competent department (MCIT unit) before launch, plus guardian express consent for a service 'directed at children'.
No game-participation conditioned on excess data (Art. 17(5)) - aligns with ATHAR's data-minimisation design.
Transfers to a foreign AI provider are not prohibited by the Law (Art. 15), but the Art. 16 permit for children's data may impose conditions - ask counsel.
limitations: Read from a newspaper reproduction, not the Al Meezan/Official Gazette copy (Al Meezan returns HTTP 500 to automated clients); verify wording against the gazette before formal reliance.
Ministerial decisions and the NCSA/MCIT regulatory guidelines (incl. the 72-hour breach practice reported by DLA Piper, ATH-SRC-1063) were not read; 'child' is not defined in the Law.

title_ar: قانون رقم 81 تاريخ 10/10/2018 - المعاملات الإلكترونية والبيانات ذات الطابع الشخصي (الباب الخامس: حماية البيانات ذات الطابع الشخصي)
edition_version: As in force on legiliban (linked to Decree 14115/2024); 136 articles; Book V = Arts. 85-109
title: Law No. 81 of 10 October 2018 on Electronic Transactions and Personal Data (Lebanon) - Book V, Arts. 85-109 (official text, Lebanese University Legal Informatics Center)
publisher: Centre de recherches et d'etudes en informatique juridique (CIJ), Lebanese University (legiliban.ul.edu.lb); Official Gazette No. 45, 18 Oct 2018, pp. 4546-4568
key_findings: Art. 1 defines personal data broadly (any information enabling direct or indirect identification, incl. by cross-matching sources); Art. 85: Book V applies to automated and non-automated processing; its protective rules cannot be contracted out of.

Art. 87: fair collection for legitimate, specific, explicit purposes; adequate, not excessive, accurate; Art. 88: notice duties (identity, purposes, mandatory/optional answers, recipients, access rights); Art. 90: retention only for the period stated in the declaration/licence.

Art. 91: processing revealing health, genetic identity or sexual life is prohibited save express consent, medical need, legal claims or an Art. 97 licence. Art. 97: licences from the Defence/Interior ministers (state security), the Justice minister (criminal offences and court cases) and the Health minister (health/genetic/sexual life); deemed refused after two months.

Art. 94 exempts from declaration, inter alia, educational institutions processing pupils' data for educational/administrative purposes (para. 4), processing of customers of commercial firms within their lawful activity (para. 6) and processing with the data subject's prior consent (para. 7); Art. 95: otherwise a declaration to the Ministry of Economy and Trade is required.

Arts. 96(7), 96(12) and 98(8): the declaration must name a representative of a controller resident abroad and state any transfer of personal data to another country; there is no adequacy test or transfer prohibition in Book V.

No child-specific rule and no definition of consent capacity in Book V (capacity falls back to general civil law). No breach-notification duty and no supervisory authority; enforcement via courts incl. the urgent-matters judge (Art. 102) and criminal penalties (Art. 106: LBP 1-30 million fine and/or 3 months-3 years; Art. 108 recidivism).
athar_applications: Lebanon: either rely on the Art. 94(6)/(7) exemptions (customers / prior consent) or file an Art. 95 declaration with the Ministry of Economy and Trade naming the AI-provider transfer (Art. 96(12)); counsel to choose.

Because Book V is silent on minors, use guardian consent for under-18s by default (civil-law capacity) and treat chat text as potentially revealing health data (Art. 91) - filter crisis disclosures out of logs.
Never collect data about criminal offences of real persons (Art. 97(2) licence) - case content must be fictional.
limitations: Lebanon's devaluation makes the LBP fines nominal; enforcement practice of the declaration regime and any implementing decrees were not checked.
The CIJ portal is the Lebanese University's legal database, not the Official Gazette PDF itself (gazette No. 45 / 18 Oct 2018 cited on the page).

title: Report of a study on the conformity of personal data provisions with Convention 108+ in Algeria, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco and Tunisia (CyberSouth)
authors: Council of Europe / European Union - CyberSouth joint project
key_findings: Finds that Lebanon's Law 81/2018 creates no independent supervisory authority, no consent prerequisite for processing, no breach notification and no cross-border transfer regime (only a mention of transfers in the Art. 96 declaration).
Recommends an independent authority, transfer safeguards, deterrent fines and impact assessments; notes biometric, racial, political and religious data are not covered as special categories.
athar_applications: Independent confirmation that a Lebanon launch faces low formal transfer barriers but high legal uncertainty (court enforcement only) - ATHAR should self-impose GDPR-level safeguards there.
limitations: Pre-dates the 2023 Jordanian PDPL (Jordan section obsolete); read through WebFetch summary (direct download refused); ministry naming in the study is inconsistent (Economy and Finance vs Economy and Commerce) - the Law text says Ministry of Economy and Trade (ATH-SRC-1801).

title_ar: نحو قانون حديث لحماية البيانات ذات الطابع الشخصي في لبنان
title: Towards a modern law for the protection of personal data in Lebanon (Arabic report)
authors: SKeyes Center for Media and Cultural Freedom (Samir Kassir Foundation)
publisher: SKeyes Center for Media and Cultural Freedom
key_findings: Compares Lebanon's Law 81/2018 with the GDPR and the Omani, Qatari and Tunisian laws; concludes the Lebanese provisions are outdated, do not expressly require consent and do not regulate children's consent.
Recommends a stand-alone Lebanese law with an independent authority and explicit parental consent for children under 16 (proposal, not law).
athar_applications: Signals likely direction of future Lebanese reform (parental consent, authority, breach notice) - design ATHAR's Lebanon flow to that standard now.
limitations: Advocacy/NGO report; legislative proposals are not law; article references should be checked against the official text (ATH-SRC-1801).

title: Overview of the Executive Regulations of the Egyptian Personal Data Protection Law (Ministerial Decision No. 816 of 2025)
key_findings: Reports that the Regulations make licensing/permits a structural condition of lawful processing, with fee scaling by data volume and an electronic application portal.

Reports a cross-border regime: no transfer, storage, sharing or processing outside Egypt without a licence/permit; the data subject's consent is required before any transfer save statutory exceptions; transfers only to the states named in the licence; adding a destination requires amendment; cross-border permits priced at 50% of the controller/processor licence fee.
Reports demonstrable consent mechanisms including guardian consent for children, and breach reporting through an electronic register within 72 hours.
athar_applications: Egypt: sending a teen's chat text to a foreign AI provider needs (1) a PDPC licence, (2) a cross-border permit naming the provider's country, and (3) specific consent (guardian's for children) - plan 3-6 months lead time or Egyptian/approved-country processing.
limitations: Law-firm summary; the Regulations' Arabic text (Official Gazette) was not read; article numbers not given; the PDPC portal (pdpc.gov.eg) is a JavaScript app that returned no text.

license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (site content, per page footer link)
title: Egypt: Data protection regulation in Executive Regulations of the Personal Data Protection Law (Ministerial Decision No. 816 of 2025) - policy tracker record
authors: Digital Policy Alert (St. Gallen Endowment for Prosperity through Trade)
key_findings: Records adoption of the Executive Regulations by the Minister of Communications and IT on 1 Nov 2025 (Decision 816/2025) and entry into force on 2 Nov 2025, the day after Official Gazette publication.
Tracks separate in-force entries for cross-border transfer regulation, operational licence requirement, cybersecurity, testing and organisational requirements (all 2 Nov 2025).
athar_applications: Fixes the Egyptian timeline: Regulations in force since 2 Nov 2025; with the one-year regularisation period reported by CMS (ATH-SRC-1062) enforcement exposure begins around Nov 2026 - i.e. now.
limitations: Tracker summary; full description behind sign-in; conflicts in dates between sources (CMS reported public release 25 Dec 2025) need counsel confirmation.

edition_version: Published 2 Mar 2023; page metadata dateModified 5 Dec 2025
title: Doing business in the UAE: navigating the data protection regime (Out-Law guide)
key_findings: States that the PDPL executive regulations have yet to be issued with no indication of timing, and that penalties and their nature are left to those regulations or the UAE Data Office.

Notes the PDPL applies to processing of UAE data subjects' data regardless of where the controller is established, has no legitimate-interest basis, and that DIFC (DP Law 5/2020) and ADGM (DPR 2021) have separate regimes.
athar_applications: UAE: the PDPL is in force but its transfer adequacy list, breach deadline and penalties remain undefined; rely on contract + explicit consent (Art. 23) for AI-provider transfers and follow the stricter Child Digital Safety Law (ATH-SRC-1053).
limitations: Law-firm guide; 'not yet issued' is a negative finding last updated Dec 2025 - the u.ae data-protection page (checked 27 Oct 2026) lists only Decree-Laws 44 and 45 of 2021, consistent with no regulation, but absence is not proof.

title_ar: قانون الموجبات والعقود - المواد 215-218 (الأهلية)
title: Code of Obligations and Contracts (Lebanon, 9 March 1932) - Arts. 215-218 on capacity (official text, Lebanese University CIJ)
publisher: CIJ, Lebanese University (legiliban.ul.edu.lb); Official Gazette No. 2642, 11 Apr 1932
key_findings: Art. 215: every person who has completed 18 years is capable of binding himself unless a legal text declares incapacity.

Art. 216: acts of a person wholly lacking discernment (young child) are non-existent; acts of a discerning minor are voidable only at the minor's (or representative's/heirs') instance, and for informal contracts only on proof of lesion (ghubn).
Art. 217: a minor duly authorised to trade is treated as an adult within that trade.
athar_applications: Lebanon: 16-17-year-olds are minors (voidable contracts) - subscriptions and data consents for under-18s should run through a guardian; no separate 'digital age' exists.
limitations: Capacity for personal-status matters is governed by communal laws; consent to data processing is not expressly linked to Art. 215 by Law 81/2018 - counsel to confirm.

title_ar: نظام المعاملات المدنية (المرسوم الملكي م/191)
edition_version: In force 16 Dec 2023 (WIPO Lex lists 17 Dec 2023); official translation for guidance, Arabic governs
title: Civil Transactions Law (Royal Decree No. M/191 of 29/11/1444H, 18 June 2023) (Saudi Arabia) - official English translation, Arts. 12-14, 48-51
authors: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia - Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers
publisher: Bureau of Experts, Official Translation Department (hosted by Ministry of Investment, misa.gov.sa)
key_findings: Art. 12: a fully competent person has reached majority, has full mental capacity and is not interdicted; majority is 18 years 'according to the Hijri calendar'.
Art. 13: under seven years = non-discerning; Art. 14: a discerning minor below majority is partially incompetent.

Arts. 48-51: minors are interdicted by law; dispositions of a non-discerning minor are void; a discerning minor's acts are valid if wholly beneficial, void if wholly harmful, voidable otherwise; from 15 a guardian/court may authorise financial dispositions.
athar_applications: KSA PDPL Art. 5 links consent to legal capacity (ATH-SRC-1049): under-18 (Hijri - about 17.5 Gregorian years) users need the legal guardian's consent; collect birth year and compute Hijri age conservatively.
limitations: 18 Hijri years = c. 17 years 5 months Gregorian; age-gate logic must compute it; applicability of CTL capacity rules to PDPL consent is an inference confirmed by the PDPL's reference to 'legal guardian' but should be confirmed by counsel.

title_ar: القانون المدني الأردني رقم 43 لسنة 1976
title: Civil Code No. 43 of 1976 (Jordan) - Arts. 43-45 and 118 (capacity)
publisher: WIPO Lex (Arabic PDF of the official text)
key_findings: Art. 43: a person reaching majority with full mental faculties and not interdicted has full capacity; majority is 18 full solar (Gregorian) years.
Art. 44: under seven = lacking discernment; Art. 45: discerning but below majority = partially incompetent.
Art. 118(3): age of discernment is seven full years; Art. 119: from 15, with court permission, a guardian may hand part of the minor's property and allow trade by way of trial.
athar_applications: Jordan PDPL Art. 5(a)(4) (ATH-SRC-1058) requires a parent/guardian's consent for a person lacking legal capacity: under-18 users need guardian consent.
limitations: WIPO Lex copy may not reflect later amendments; counsel to confirm.

title_ar: مرسوم بقانون رقم (7) لسنة 1986 بإصدار قانون الولاية على المال
title: Decree-Law No. (7) of 1986 promulgating the Law on Guardianship over Property (Bahrain) - Art. 13 (age of majority)
publisher: Legislation & Legal Opinion Commission (LLOC), Kingdom of Bahrain
key_findings: Art. 13: the age of majority is 21 full Gregorian years; a person reaching it has full capacity unless guardianship was extended or an impediment arises.
Art. 14: guardianship over a minor's property belongs to the father, then the paternal grandfather.
Read with Civil Code (LD 19/2001) Arts. 72-75 (ATH-SRC-1811): under seven lacks discretion; a discerning minor's dispositions are voidable until 'legal age'.
athar_applications: Bahrain PDPL Art. 24 (ATH-SRC-1059) requires consent from a person of full capacity, else the guardian: on this text, users aged 18-20 in Bahrain may also need guardian consent - a major difference from all other target markets; counsel must confirm before launch.
limitations: Amendment history page on LLOC returned no amendment list; a later law may have lowered the age - not found in this session; counsel to confirm the current rule and its interaction with the PDPL.

title_ar: القانون المدني البحريني - مرسوم بقانون رقم 19 لسنة 2001
title: Civil Code promulgated by Legislative Decree No. 19 of 2001 (Bahrain), as amended to Law No. 27 of 2017 - English translation, Arts. 72-77
key_findings: Art. 72: every person not declared incapable has capacity to contract; Art. 73: a minor lacking discretion has no capacity and every person under seven lacks discretion.

Art. 74: a discerning minor's dispositions are valid if wholly beneficial, void if wholly detrimental, and annullable if mixed unless ratified at legal age or by the guardian/Minors Estate Guardianship Council.
Art. 75: a minor has discretion from the age of discretion until attaining 'legal age' (fixed at 21 by ATH-SRC-1810).
athar_applications: Treat Bahraini users under 21 as minors for contract/consent purposes pending counsel.
limitations: Translation; Arabic prevails.

title_ar: القانون المدني المصري رقم 131 لسنة 1948
title: Civil Code No. 131 of 1948 (Egypt) - Arts. 44-46 (capacity)
publisher: WIPO Lex (Arabic PDF, amended to Law No. 55 of 1970)
key_findings: Art. 44: full capacity at majority; majority is 21 full Gregorian years.
Art. 45: under seven = lacking discernment; Art. 46: discerning but below majority = partially incompetent.
Art. 42(2): a minor of 18 may have a special domicile for acts the law lets him perform.
athar_applications: Egypt: data protection law treats 'child' data as sensitive (Law 151/2020 Art. 12, ATH-SRC-1061); the civil majority is 21, so 18-20-year-olds may be adults for data law (child = under 18 per Child Law, ATH-SRC-1814) but not for some contracts - require guardian consent for subscriptions under 21 until counsel advises.
limitations: WIPO copy amended only to 1970; Law 118/1952 (guardianship over property) also governs - not read; counsel to confirm.

title_ar: القانون المدني الكويتي - مرسوم بالقانون رقم 67 لسنة 1980
title: Civil Code - Decree-Law No. 67 of 1980 (Kuwait) - Arts. 84-96 (capacity)
publisher: ICNL Online Library (reproduction of the GCC legal portal text)
key_findings: Art. 96: full capacity at majority, which is 21 full Gregorian years.
Art. 86: a non-discerning minor has no capacity; anyone under seven is non-discerning; Art. 87: a discerning minor's acts are valid if purely beneficial, void if purely harmful, voidable otherwise.
Art. 88: from 18 a guardian may permit a discerning minor to manage his property; Art. 95: from 18 a discerning minor may make a will.
athar_applications: Kuwait: CITRA regulation requires written guardian consent for under-18s (ATH-SRC-1060) but civil majority is 21 - paid subscriptions by 18-20-year-olds may be voidable; counsel to confirm.
limitations: ICNL copy printed from gcc-legal.org in 2016; later amendments not checked; not the official gazette.

title_ar: قانون الطفل المصري رقم 12 لسنة 1996 المعدل بالقانون رقم 126 لسنة 2008
title: Child Law No. 12 of 1996 as amended by Law No. 126 of 2008 (Egypt) - Arts. 2, 94-95, 122, 125-127 (Arabic text, CRIN archive)
publisher: Child Rights International Network (CRIN) archive - Arabic text by chapter
key_findings: Art. 2: a 'child' for the Law's purposes is anyone who has not exceeded 18 full Gregorian years.
Art. 94: no criminal responsibility for a child not exceeding 12 full Gregorian years; for ages 7-12 the Child Court alone may impose protective measures.

Art. 122: Juvenile (Child) Courts have exclusive jurisdiction over accused children, with exceptions for over-15s tried with adults for felonies; Art. 125: mandatory lawyer in felonies and imprisonable misdemeanours; Art. 126: closed hearings - only relatives, witnesses, lawyers, social monitors; Art. 127: social/psychological file before disposal.
athar_applications: Egypt-set cases: a teen suspect is processed by Child Prosecution/Child Court, with a lawyer and social worker, in a closed hearing - stories must not show public trials or media naming of minors.
limitations: CRIN archive reproduction (2008 consolidation); amendments by Laws 6 and 7 of 2015 (listed by Manshurat) not reviewed; Manshurat's PDF is image-only.

title_ar: مرسوم سلطاني رقم 29/2013 بإصدار قانون المعاملات المدنية
title: Royal Decree No. 29/2013 promulgating the Civil Transactions Law (Oman) - Arts. 41-43 (capacity)
key_findings: Art. 41: full capacity at majority; majority is completion of 18 years of age.
Art. 42: age of discernment is seven full years; Art. 43: discerning but below majority = partially incompetent.
Art. 39(2): a minor of 15 may have a special domicile for acts the law permits.
athar_applications: Oman PDPL Art. 6 (ATH-SRC-1056) requires guardian consent for a 'child'; the PDPL does not define child, but Child Law RD 22/2014 (ATH-SRC-1816) and the civil majority both point to under-18.
limitations: Qanoon.om is a widely used database rather than the Official Gazette; calendar (Hijri/Gregorian) not stated in Art. 41 - Child Law specifies Gregorian.

title_ar: مرسوم سلطاني رقم 22/2014 بإصدار قانون الطفل
title: Royal Decree No. 22/2014 promulgating the Child Law (Oman) - Art. 1 definitions
key_findings: Art. 1(d): a child is every human who has not completed 18 years by the Gregorian calendar.
The Law defines a child protection delegate (mandoub) role - closes wave-1 gap on the definition of 'child' for Oman's PDPL Art. 6 guardian-consent rule (inference: PDPL itself has no definition).
athar_applications: Oman: guardian consent for every user under 18 Gregorian years.
limitations: Cross-application of the Child Law definition to the PDPL is an interpretation; the PDPL Executive Regulation (ATH-SRC-1057) may define it - not found in the sections read.

title_ar: مدونة الأسرة المغربية 2004
title: The Moroccan Family Code (Moudawana) of 5 February 2004 - unofficial English translation (Global Rights), Arts. 209-214
publisher: FAOLEX (FAO legal database) - Global Rights translation
key_findings: Art. 209: the age of legal majority is 18 complete Gregorian years.
Art. 214: a discerning young person is one who has completed 12 full Gregorian years (higher than the seven-year threshold in the Mashriq codes).
athar_applications: Morocco: under-18s need a legal representative for contracts and, by inference, for consent under Law 09-08 (ATH-SRC-1818).
limitations: Unofficial translation; a family-code reform was under discussion in 2024-2026 - not checked; Arabic text prevails.

title_ar: القانون رقم 09.08 المتعلق بحماية الأشخاص الذاتيين تجاه معالجة المعطيات ذات الطابع الشخصي
edition_version: Dahir No. 1-09-15 of 18 Feb 2009; Official Bulletin No. 5714 of 5 Mar 2009
title: Law No. 09-08 on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data (Morocco) - text summary and CNDP portal
publisher: Upsilon Consulting (text page); CNDP (cndp.ma) official portal
key_findings: Art. 4: prior consent principle with exceptions (legal obligation, contract, vital interests, public interest, legitimate interest); no child-specific rule reported.
Arts. 12-20 prior declaration to the CNDP; Arts. 21-22 prior authorisation for sensitive data, national ID processing, interconnection and international transfers.
Arts. 43-44: transfers abroad only to states ensuring adequate protection, otherwise CNDP authorisation with safeguards; CNDP portal offers a dedicated 'notify a transfer abroad' procedure.
Penalties (Arts. 51-66): e.g. MAD 10,000-100,000 for failure to declare/obtain authorisation (Art. 52); fines doubled for legal entities (Art. 64).
athar_applications: Morocco: declaration to CNDP + transfer authorisation before sending chat text to a non-adequate country; guardian consent for under-18s by civil-law capacity (ATH-SRC-1817).
limitations: Official Arabic text (adala.justice.gov.ma) unreachable from this environment (connection reset); article content from a consultancy page confirmed in structure by CNDP's portal; counsel must read the Bulletin Officiel text.

title_ar: بلاغ صحفي: الذكاء الاصطناعي وحماية المعطيات ذات الطابع الشخصي
title: CNDP press release: Artificial intelligence and personal data protection (18 March 2025)
authors: Commission Nationale de controle de la protection des Donnees a caractere Personnel (CNDP), Morocco
key_findings: States that AI processing of personal data is governed by Law 09-08 and that automated decisions need special attention (fairness, transparency, trust, readability).
Announces work on a CNDP deliberation (mudawala) on AI processing and public hearings with experts, institutions and civil society.
athar_applications: Morocco: expect an AI-specific CNDP deliberation; design ATHAR's AI scoring as non-decisive (no automated decisions with significant effects on minors).
limitations: Press release only; whether the deliberation was issued by Oct 2026 was not verified.

title_ar: قانون أصول المحاكمات الجزائية اللبناني رقم 328 تاريخ 2/8/2001
edition_version: As amended (incl. Art. 11 bis environmental prosecutor)
title: Code of Criminal Procedure, Law No. 328 of 2 August 2001 (Lebanon) - Arts. 1-4, 11-12, 51-61, 74-81, 85-97 (official text, Lebanese University CIJ)
publisher: CIJ, Lebanese University (legiliban.ul.edu.lb); Official Gazette No. 38, 7 Aug 2001
key_findings: Two-step model: the Public Prosecution (Arts. 11-12) brings the public action; an Investigating Judge (Arts. 51-54, 59-60) investigates 'objectively' once seized by a prosecution claim or a victim's direct complaint, and may not then sit in judgment; the Indictment Chamber (Art. 54, 128 ff.) is the appeal body and alone indicts for felonies.
Art. 53: the investigation is secret until referral to trial (except the indictment decision); disclosure is an offence.

Arts. 76-79: at first appearance the judge must state the charge and evidence and inform the defendant of the right to a lawyer - omission voids the interrogation as evidence; Art. 77: free will must be respected; a silent defendant may not be compelled to speak; Art. 79: lawyer-client communications are confidential and evidence obtained by breaching that is inadmissible.

Art. 91: minors under 18 are heard 'for information' (not as sworn witnesses); a sworn statement by a minor over 15 is not void and he is not prosecuted for perjury; close relatives of the defendant are barred from testifying (heard only for information).
athar_applications: Lebanon-set stories: the 'detective' is never the decision-maker - realism requires a prosecutor and an investigating judge; a teen witness gives information, not sworn testimony; investigation files are secret (no leaking dossiers to the teen hero).
Teaching moment: illegally obtained statements are void - supports ATHAR's anti-coercion design (KO on ethical interviewing).
limitations: Principle-level reading of selected chapters; later amendments (e.g. Law 191/2020 on detention safeguards) not reviewed; not legal advice.

title_ar: قانون رقم 422 تاريخ 6/6/2002 - حماية الأحداث المخالفين للقانون أو المعرضين للخطر
title: Law No. 422 of 6 June 2002 on the Protection of Juveniles in Conflict with the Law or at Risk (Lebanon) - Arts. 1-4, 30-50 (official text, Lebanese University CIJ)
publisher: CIJ, Lebanese University; Official Gazette No. 34, 13 Jun 2002
key_findings: Art. 1: a juvenile is a person under 18 who commits an offence or is at risk; Art. 3: no criminal prosecution of a child under seven at the time of the act.
Art. 2: guiding principles - special assistance, the juvenile's interest, fair and humane treatment, diversion and non-custodial measures where possible.

Art. 34: when a juvenile is brought before the prosecution/judicial police, parents and an accredited social delegate must be notified and the delegate must attend the investigation; Art. 42: a lawyer is mandatory in felony trials.

Art. 40: juvenile trials are held in camera; Art. 48: publishing the juvenile's picture or the facts of the investigation/trial is prohibited (final judgment may be published with initials only), on pain of 3 months-1 year and a fine.
athar_applications: A Lebanese teen-detective story may not show a minor suspect's photo, name or case details being published; any minor questioned is accompanied by a social delegate and family.
limitations: Amended Art. 31 text appears twice on the portal (consolidation artefact); measures (Arts. 5-29) not reviewed in detail.

title_ar: قانون الإجراءات الجنائية رقم 174 لسنة 2025
edition_version: Issuing article 6 amended by Law 160 of 2026 (30 Sep 2026): in force from 1 Oct 2027; until then the 1950 Code of Criminal Procedure (No. 150/1950) remains applicable
title: Criminal Procedure Law No. 174 of 2025 (Egypt) - full text with Law No. 160 of 2026 postponement (Manshurat)
authors: Arab Republic of Egypt - House of Representatives
key_findings: Art. 1: the Public Prosecution conducts the investigation and initiates and pursues the criminal action; others may do so only where the law provides.

Arts. 174-175: the Prosecution (or the accused/civil party, or the Minister of Justice via the Court of Appeal) may request appointment of an investigating judge where circumstances make it more suitable; the judge then has exclusive competence (Art. 176 ff.).
Art. 5: where the victim is under 15 (or mentally disordered), a complaint is lodged by the person holding guardianship.
Issuing art. 6 as amended in Sept 2026 postpones entry into force to 1 October 2027 (confirmed by a parliamentary news report of the Legislative Committee, 27 Oct 2026).
athar_applications: Egypt-set stories: the investigating authority is the Niyaba (Public Prosecution) - not police detectives and not, normally, an investigating judge; ATHAR scripts for 2026-27 should describe the current 1950 Code's roles (same Niyaba-led model).
limitations: Secondary database copy, not the Official Gazette; the 1950 Code currently in force was not read article by article; principle-level only.

title_ar: «التشريعية» تحسم موقفها.. أكتوبر 2027 موعداً لتطبيق قانون الإجراءات الجنائية
title: Parliamentary report: Legislative Committee sets October 2027 for applying the Criminal Procedure Law (Parlmany, Youm7 group)
key_findings: Reports the House Constitutional and Legislative Affairs Committee approved amending Law 174/2025 so it applies from October 2027, to complete organisational, technical and human-resource readiness.
athar_applications: Date anchor for Egyptian procedural realism in content written 2026-2027.
limitations: News report; the amending Law No. 160/2026 is reflected in Manshurat's consolidated text (ATH-SRC-1822).

title_ar: نظام الإجراءات الجزائية (المرسوم الملكي م/39)
title: Law of Criminal Procedure, Royal Decree No. M/39 of 28/7/1422H (16 Oct 2001) (Saudi Arabia) - English translation, Arts. 1-4, 13-14, 102
publisher: WIPO Lex (English translation); Umm al-Qura Gazette No. 3867, 3 Nov 2001
key_findings: Art. 1: courts apply Shari'ah principles and state laws not contradicting them; Art. 2: no arrest, search or detention except as provided by law and no bodily/moral harm, torture or degrading treatment.

Art. 3: no penal punishment except for a prohibited act and after conviction by a final judgment following a Shari'ah-compliant trial (functional presumption of innocence; the Basic Law has no express clause in the text read).

Art. 4: right to a lawyer in investigation and trial; Arts. 14 ff.: the Bureau of Investigation and Prosecution (now the Public Prosecution) investigates and prosecutes; Art. 102: interrogation must not affect the accused's will, no oath, no coercive measures.
Art. 13: juveniles are investigated and tried under the relevant laws and regulations (Juveniles Law 1439H, ATH-SRC-1825).
athar_applications: KSA-set stories: the Public Prosecution (Niyaba) investigates; police gather evidence under its supervision; no coerced confessions - align character dialogue with Art. 102.
limitations: Translation of the 2001 text; superseding implementing regulations and the 2017 renaming of the Bureau to the Public Prosecution not reflected; principle-level only.

title: Thomson Reuters Enterprise Centre GmbH v. ROSS Intelligence Inc., No. 25-2153 (3d Cir. Sept. 29, 2026) (precedential opinion)
authors: United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit (Montgomery-Reeves, J.; Restrepo and Bove, JJ.)
publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
key_findings: Affirms the D. Del. partial summary judgment: the 2,243 Westlaw headnotes clear the low Feist originality bar (merger doctrine rejected), and ROSS's copying to train a non-generative legal-research AI was not fair use.

Factor one: same ultimate purpose (a legal-research platform) - training was an intermediate step giving at most a slight difference in use; 'minimally transformative, at best'; ROSS did not need the headnotes because the opinions were freely available ('ease is not a justification for copying').
Factor four: ROSS built a direct commercial substitute; a market for licensing such content as AI training data is developing and was usurped.

The court expressly confines the ruling: ROSS was not generative AI; footnote 7 distinguishes Bartz and the OpenAI MDL and notes a DOJ Statement of Interest (S.D.N.Y., 1 Sep 2026) arguing LLM training is transformative. Key Number System originality not decided (not briefed).
athar_applications: First US appellate AI-training decision: copying a competitor's curated content to build a competing educational/reference product is the highest-risk pattern - ATHAR must not train or ground on rival mystery-learning or curriculum products' proprietary materials.
Confirms the licensing-market argument: datasets licensed for AI training have value; ATHAR's corpus policy (Tier A only) stands.
limitations: Non-generative system; outcome on generative training remains open (Bartz/Kadrey district rulings; OpenAI MDL pending).

National rating regimes can block distribution per territory through 'refused classification' - a channel through which Saudi Gmedia now acts on IARC storefronts.
limitations: Help page does not (yet) list Gmedia/Saudi as a mapped authority despite IARC's 2026 milestone - mapping may lag; Apple uses its own rating system (ATH-SRC-1066).

title_ar: ما الضوابط العامة للفسح عن الألعاب الإلكترونية في السعودية؟
title: What are the general controls for clearing (fash) electronic games in Saudi Arabia? (Saudipedia)
key_findings: Clearance of electronic games for commercial establishments requires a prior Saudi age rating from the Authority, two sealed copies bearing the rating, a valid commercial registration and an import/distribution licence; one clearance per platform.
Rating and clearance are processed through the 'I'lam' media services platform, which also covers licensing for streaming, podcasts, digital content production, e-games and electronic publications.
athar_applications: The physical-goods clearance (fash) model targets retail/imported games; a digital-only educational app distributed via app stores is reached through IARC (ATH-SRC-1846) and possibly through media-activity licensing if ATHAR has a Saudi entity - counsel/Gmedia to confirm.
limitations: Encyclopaedia summary; does not address apps distributed only via app stores or educational apps; publication date not shown (inferred 2024+).

title_ar: «تنظيم الإعلام» تحذّر من التهاون في التصنيف العمري للألعاب الإلكترونية
title: 'Media Regulation' warns against laxity in age classification of electronic games (Okaz, 2 Sep 2025)
key_findings: Reports a GMedia statement that compliance with e-game age classification is a statutory duty and that violations will be subject to regulatory procedures; frames parental awareness as the first line of defence (bullying, grooming).
athar_applications: Signals active Saudi enforcement interest in age ratings for games - ATHAR should obtain a rating before any KSA marketing.
limitations: Press report of a statement; no legal citation; scope (apps vs boxed games) unclear.

title: A comprehensive regulatory framework for media content violations: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 42 of 2025
key_findings: Cabinet Decision No. 42 of 2025 (in force 29 May 2025) sets administrative violations and fines (AED 5,000-1,000,000) under Federal Decree-Law No. 55 of 2023 on Media Regulation and its implementing regulation; applies to individuals, media institutions and platforms operating in the UAE, including free zones.

Content violations include 'failure to adhere to age classifications or national identity in content' (AED 5,000-100,000) and 'violation of privacy or children's rights' (AED 5,000-100,000); a Committee for Violations of Media Content Standards assesses content breaches; Cabinet Decision No. 41 of 2025 sets licence types and fees.
athar_applications: UAE: if ATHAR is a 'media activity' in the UAE (e-games/digital content), mislabelled age classification is directly finable - align the store rating, in-app age labels and marketing.
limitations: Law-firm summary; Decree-Law 55/2023 and its executive regulation not read directly (uaelegislation.gov.ae blocks automated access); whether a foreign app without UAE presence 'operates within the UAE' is a counsel question.

title: Media Law and Advertising Standards in the UAE: Key Rules and Restrictions (Al Tamimi & Company)
key_findings: Federal Decree-Law No. 55 of 2023 on Media Regulation in force since 1 Dec 2023; its Executive Regulation effective since 31 Oct 2024; the law covers audio, visual, electronic and digital media and electronic games.

The UAE Media Council sets age-rating criteria; media content standards include no incitement to violence/hatred (std 9), no incitement to commit crimes or encouragement of murder, rape or drug use (std 13), and no content violating public morals or offending young people (std 14).
Licensing described for UAE-established entities (trade licence + Media Council licence/permit, renewed yearly); the article is silent on foreign digital platforms.
athar_applications: Content rules map onto ATHAR's case-design gates: crimes must never be glamorised or presented as instructions (std 13); age labels must follow Media Council criteria for UAE users.
limitations: Read through WebFetch summary (site JS-gated); no article numbers; the Media Council's game age-classification guide itself remains unread (G02 gap persists).

title: Bahrain issues new privacy guidelines supplementing the Personal Data Protection Law (Ministerial Resolutions Nos. 42-46 of 2022)
key_findings: Ten ministerial resolutions of 17 Mar 2022 supplement the PDPL. Resolution 42/2022 sets an Adequacy List of 83 countries incl. UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Jordan, Kuwait, Egypt, India, all EU states, UK and USA - transfers there need no PDPA authorisation; others need case-by-case authorisation (with a copy of the contract) or approved 'Corporate Rules'.

Resolution 43/2022: technical/organisational measures incl. privacy by design, DPIAs in certain cases and breach notification to the PDPA within 72 hours of awareness unless unlikely to result in risk; data subjects informed in certain cases.

Resolution 44: notification/prior-authorisation procedures (PDPL Arts. 14-15); Resolution 45: sensitive data rules; Resolution 46: optional Data Protection Guardian (mandatory cases left to a later resolution).
athar_applications: Bahrain closes wave-1 gaps: breach notice 72 h; sending chat text to a US/EU AI provider is a transfer to an adequate country (no PDPA authorisation) - the main Bahrain issue is capacity (majority 21, ATH-SRC-1810) and the Art. 14 notification.
limitations: Law-firm summary of 2022 resolutions; resolution texts and any later amendments of the adequacy list not read.

title: Saudi Arabia sets guidelines for using AI in education (Ministry of Education + SDAIA guidebook) - Gulf News, 26 Jan 2025; Okaz, 25 Jan 2025
key_findings: The Ministry of Education, with SDAIA, issued a three-part guidebook on generative AI in education for students, teachers and parents, aligned with SDAIA and National eLearning Center guidance.
Reported rules: generative AI tools are not to be used by students under 13 except under direct supervision, and students under 18 may not use them without clear parental consent.
athar_applications: KSA schools channel: ATHAR's AI characters for 13-17 require explicit parental consent (matches PDPL guardian consent); under-13 only in teacher-supervised classroom mode - out of MVP scope.
limitations: Press reports; the guidebook itself (MoE PDF) not read; the age rules are attributed by Gulf News to Al Yaum newspaper - verify against the official guide before relying.

title: UAE sets strict new rules on generative AI in schools, banning use for under-13s (Ministry of Education 2026 'Safe and Responsible Use of AI in Classrooms' manual) - Gulf News, 14 Feb 2026
key_findings: The UAE Ministry of Education's 2026 manual prohibits generative AI tools for students under 13 or below Year 7, allows use only with direct teacher oversight, bans unapproved GenAI platforms and creating external student accounts without permission.

Prohibits inputting any personal data of students, teachers or parents (names, photos, audio/video, ID, contacts) into AI systems; bans content contrary to religious/national/cultural values or containing violence, disturbing imagery, hate speech or harmful psychological content.
Emarat Al Youm (4 Sep 2026) reports schools enforcing these controls at the start of 2026-2027.
athar_applications: UAE school sales require: Ministry-approved platform status, teacher-supervised AI interactions, no student PII sent to the AI (pseudonymous IDs only), and Grade 7+ only - these are product requirements, not just policies.
ATHAR's AI-character 'violence' must stay non-graphic and non-disturbing to pass school content rules.
limitations: Press report of an official manual not read directly; applies to schools (MoE system), not consumer apps used at home.

title_ar: إجراءات مدرسية لضبط استخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي التوليدي في الصفوف
title: School measures to control generative AI use in classrooms (Emarat Al Youm, 4 Sep 2026)
key_findings: Reports that at the start of 2026-27 UAE schools tightened controls for students under 13, banned unapproved GenAI tools in class, blocked VPN access to unauthorised platforms and prohibited creating student accounts on external services requiring personal data.
athar_applications: Expect UAE schools to require SSO/rostered accounts and data-processing agreements rather than students self-registering.
limitations: News report; school practice varies by emirate and school type.

title: Criminal Procedures in UAE - overview of Federal Decree-Law No. 38 of 2022 and rights of the accused (Embassy of India, Abu Dhabi)
publisher: Embassy of India in the UAE (indembassyuae.gov.in)
key_findings: Under Federal Decree-Law No. 38 of 2022 (CPL), criminal actions are generally instituted and prosecuted by the Public Prosecution (and the Attorney General); Judicial Police Officers include Public Prosecution members and police officers.

Art. 48: before statements, the arrested person is told the charge and the right to remain silent; referral to the Public Prosecution within 48 hours, which must question within 24 hours and decide on remand or release; Art. 52-56 search rules (home search needs a written Prosecution warrant except in flagrante delicto).

Art. 97: on first presentation the Prosecutor records identity, informs of the charge and records answers; Art. 98: defence counsel may attend and review papers unless the Prosecutor decides otherwise for the investigation.
athar_applications: UAE-set stories: police gather evidence, the Niyaba investigates and questions; searches need warrants; the suspect is told of the right to silence - ATHAR's 'teen detective' gathers information and hands it to authorities, never searches homes or interrogates.
limitations: Government (foreign mission) explanatory note, not the law text (uaelegislation.gov.ae blocks automated access); article numbers as cited by the Embassy; principle-level.

edition_version: Produced Nov 2014; may have been edited by CRIN
title: Access to Justice for Children: Qatar
authors: DLA Piper (for Child Rights International Network, CRIN)
key_findings: Reports Qatar Civil Code (Law No. 22 of 2004): discretion at seven (Art. 50); persons between discretion and majority lack capacity; age of majority 18 (Art. 49); minors are under natural or legal guardianship (Art. 52).
Reports guardianship over a minor's property belongs to the father, then the paternal grandfather (Law No. 40 of 2004, Art. 4); Constitution Art. 22 obliges the State to protect the young.
athar_applications: Qatar: under-18 users need the guardian (wali) for consent; matches Law 13/2016 Art. 17 guardian-consent rule (ATH-SRC-1800).
limitations: Secondary (2014); the Civil Code text was not read; counsel to confirm and check later amendments.

title_ar: الإمارات.. خفض سن الرشد إلى 18 سنة والقاصر إلى 15 سنة يدخل حيز التنفيذ
title: UAE: age of majority lowered to 18 and minor's authorisation age to 15 as new Civil Transactions Law No. 25 of 2025 enters into force (Al Bayan, 1 Jun 2026)
key_findings: Reports that the new Civil Transactions Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025) entered into force on Monday 1 June 2026, lowering the age of majority from 21 lunar (Hijri) years to 18 Gregorian years.
Reports the age at which a discerning minor may seek permission to manage his property moved from 18 Hijri to 15 Gregorian years (court-authorised acts).
athar_applications: UAE: from 1 Jun 2026 users aged 18+ (Gregorian) have full capacity - guardian consent needed for under-18s only (Child Digital Safety Law adds verifiable parental consent for under-13s, ATH-SRC-1053).
limitations: Press report; the Decree-Law text (uaelegislation.gov.ae) could not be fetched (Cloudflare block / WebFetch client error); article numbers unknown.

title: Officially: Roblox blocked in Egypt (Emarat Al Youm, 2 Feb 2026)
title_ar: رسميًا.. حجب لعبة روبلوكس في مصر
key_findings: Reports that Egypt's Supreme Council for Media Regulation decided (Sunday, 1 Feb 2026) to officially block the Roblox platform to protect children's moral and educational values and limit psychological/behavioural harms, as announced by its chairman Essam El-Amir.
Reports a Senate proposal to regulate online-game platforms in general.
athar_applications: Egypt: there is no IARC-style national rating, but the media regulator can block a game/platform outright on child-protection grounds - ATHAR needs a child-safety dossier and a regulator-relations plan before Egyptian scale-up; no user-to-user chat or UGC in the Egypt build.
limitations: News report; the Council's legal basis (Law 180/2018) and decision text not read.
